messages:
AcmeOncall: Hey team — we're seeing a sharp spike of 5xx and timeouts hitting the hosted inference API from our EU customers. Started ~10:31 UTC, mostly us-east-1 AZ 'a'. Request failures look like 502/504/gateway timeouts. Can someone triage?

SupportBot: Auto-ticket created #INC-4829. Linking oncall. Priority: P1 if customer impact confirmed. :rotating_light:

Maya: Thanks. Can you paste one example request id and sample headers? Also which model/route they were hitting?

AcmeOncall: Request id: req_8f7c3a. Route: /v1/generate (hosted-prod-us). Model: gpt-open-13b (default variant). Attached logs show repeated TLS handshakes then connection reset.

AJ: I'm seeing increased 5xx rates in us-east-1a at the edge LB. 15-20% packet loss on control-plane to inference nodes in that AZ. Other AZs look normal.

Sophie: +1. Cloud provider console shows network flaps reported on a subset of spine switches in us-east-1a. They flagged a maintenance event and some BGP session churn.

Nate: Running quick repro: `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'` — getting `502 Bad Gateway` intermittently, large TCP retransmits.

Luis: Ran mtr from edge-proxy-12 to inference-node-7 in us-east-1a:```
Start: mtr -r -c 50 inference-node-7
 1. 10.0.0.1    0.0%
 2. 10.0.1.1    5.0%
 3. 203.0.113.7 60.0%  (provider-asn)
 4. 198.51.100.2 58.0%
 5. 198.51.100.5 0.0%
---
Packet loss concentrated on hop 3 (external provider).
```

InfraBot: Observability alert: cross-AZ latency spike > 400ms for us-east-1a -> us-east-1b traffic; backend 5xx rate up 18% over baseline.

Maya: Ok looks like provider-level issue affecting that AZ's path. Action plan: 1) Fail traffic away from us-east-1a for hosted API routes (soft failover) 2) Notify customers (support) 3) Engage cloud provider with traces + BGP logs 4) If needed, enable route-level fallback to model-variant in other region.

AJ: Starting soft-failover: updating routing policy to prefer us-east-1b with weighted 90/10. I'll keep 10% to test degradations.

Sophie: I'll open a channel with provider support (case #PROV-9982) and attach mtr/traceroutes and BGP session flaps.

AcmeOncall: Appreciate the quick action. Will monitor from our side. We may need a short maintenance window if customers see persistent errors.

Nate: FYI I'm forcing a canary to us-east-1b only for the model-gpt-open-13b route:```json
POST /admin/route-update
{
  "route": "/v1/generate",
  "model": "gpt-open-13b",
  "policy": { "primary": "us-east-1b", "weights": {"us-east-1b": 1.0} },
  "reason": "AZ network flap us-east-1a"
}
```

Luis: After the traffic shift 5xx rates dropped to baseline in the next 3 minutes for the affected route. Latency normalized for the customers rerouted.

SupportBot: Notifying affected customers: message queued to all projects with traffic through us-east-1a (Affected window: 10:31-10:55 UTC).

Sophie: Provider responded: they've observed fiber congestion and are rerouting via alternate POPs, BGP session restart at 10:38 UTC. They estimate full convergence in ~20-30 mins.

Maya: Good. Keep the soft-failover active until provider confirms. Also add an extra health check and reduce connection keepalive to shorten teardown time.

AJ: Implementing health check change across edge LBs: `timeout 10s, interval 5s` and lowering keepalive to 30s. Pushing now.

AcmeOncall: We're still seeing occasional 504s but much reduced. Thanks for the quick failover. Any risk to cached KV entries or sessions?

Luis: No KV impact; stateful model caches are per-AZ but we've preserved session affinity for routed requests. There's a small Recompute cost due to rehydration on other AZ nodes (expected).

InfraBot: Provider alert: BGP convergence complete at 10:57 UTC. Packet loss reduced to <1% on previously affected path.

Nate: Rolling back the forced 100% to us-east-1b -> switching to weight 70/30 (b/a) to test incremental move back.

Sophie: Provider confirmed root cause: a transit provider had upstream flaps during a maintenance window and some sessions were black-holing traffic to us-east-1a. They've issued postmortem and are scheduling a follow-up. Case closed on provider side.

SupportBot: Customers updated with final status and mitigation steps. Ticket INC-4829 marked resolved (monitoring phase).

Maya: Summary for postmortem thread: cause = provider transit BGP/session flaps causing packet loss to us-east-1a -> 5xx/timeouts. Impact = hosted API 502/504 for customers routed to that AZ between 10:31-10:57 UTC. Mitigation = soft-failover routing to us-east-1b, reduced LB keepalive/health-check tuning, provider engagement. Action items: 1) Add automated zone failover runbook, 2) Improve endpoint-level health metrics, 3) Add synthetic tracing across provider paths. Assign to Nate/Luis/Sophie.

Maya: Any objections to closing incident and opening a postmortem?

AcmeOncall: No objections. Thanks everyone. :heart:

Luis: I'll start the postmortem doc and link it here when ready.

InfraBot: Incident auto-closure scheduled in 24h if no regressions detected.

Maya: Closing thread — moving to postmortem and lessons-learned. Great job on the rapid routing mitigation. :thumbsup:
